🔥 GATE 2027 Original: Databases - B+ Tree Indexing

A B+ tree index is constructed on a relation with search key size = 16 bytes, record pointer = 8 bytes, block pointer = 8 bytes, and block size = 1024 bytes. What is the maximum number of search keys that can be accommodated in a leaf node of this B+ tree, assuming the leaf node includes one block pointer to the next leaf?

💡 Detailed Concept & Solution:
In a leaf node of a B+ tree, each entry consists of (Search Key, Record Pointer). In addition, there is one next-leaf block pointer.
Let $p$ be the number of keys in the leaf node.
Total size $= p \times (\text{Key Size} + \text{Record Pointer Size}) + \text{Next Block Pointer} \le \text{Block Size}$
$p \times (16 + 8) + 8 \le 1024$
$p \times 24 + 8 \le 1024 \implies 24p \le 1016 \implies p \le \lfloor 1016 / 24 \rfloor = 42.33$
Maximum number of keys = 42.

Query I

  1. SELECT name, MIN(age)
  2. FROM Alums
  3. WHERE state = “CA”;

Query II

  1. SELECT name, age
  2. FROM Alums
  3. WHERE state = “CA”
  4.         AND age <= ALL (SELECT age FROM Alums
  5.                         WHERE state = “CA”);

  1. SELECT name, age
  2. FROM Alums
  3. WHERE state = “CA”
  4.         AND age = (SELECT  MIN(age) FROM Alums);
